1.4.summary: Press feel is reworked. Owner-visible on the phone: (1) Ticks happen when a tap completes, not when the finger lands. A finger that lands on a card and turns into a scroll ticks nothing and shows no shrink. A tap that is lifted early still shrinks and ticks once. (2) The give starts only after 60 ms (PRESS_DELAY, exported from Press.tsx). A quick tap still shows it, because Pressability delivers press-in and press-out together on release. (3) Segmented ticks the instant a finger lands on the segment that would change, and ticks nothing on the already chosen one. In a scrolling rail (scroll prop) the tick waits for release, because a drag may be starting. (4) A long press ticks when it fires, so the chat-bubble and group-message menus keep their tick. A tap on a surface with no onPress ticks nothing. (5) Settled list rows no longer carry a Reanimated view. Press with scaleTo={1} (TaskCard and ApplicationFace body/foot, Agreement body/foot) is a plain Pressable with no shared value or animated style. Appear renders a plain View for rows that mounted settled; only arriving rows keep the animated view. Code: Press now follows the ladder (default sys.motion.scale.button, equal to pressScale 0.97) and has a new hapticOn prop, 'in' | 'release' with default 'release'. Press chooses StaticPress or GivingPress once at mount. usePressLift() is the single give/settle/lift (shared value, style, give, settle; default rung sys.motion.scale.row 0.985); Press itself uses it, and TaskCard, ApplicationFace and AgreementCollectionPresentation adopt it in later waves. Appear latches its mode and entrance at mount. The new ROWS_THAT_ARRIVE=6 is exported. useAppear().settle(keys, viewKey, {afterLoading}) lets the first list after a skeleton arrive once, capped at 6 rows; a warm return and a filter change stay still. No adopter passes the option yet.

decisions: Press default reads sys.motion.scale.button (the ladder), not the legacy pressScale; both are 0.97 and the test pins the equality.

The 60 ms delay is Pressable's own unstable_pressDelay, not a JS timer. It is skipped when hapticOn is 'in' (the tick answers at once), and a caller's own unstable_pressDelay wins. A side effect is that the caller's onPressIn, including the card give() in TaskCard/ApplicationFace/Agreement, now arrives 60 ms after touch-down.

PRESS_DELAY lives in Press.tsx because tokens.ts is item 1.2's file; it should become sys.motion.pressDelay later. The audit called the delay optional, and I took it because 'does not shrink' on a scroll needs it.
Release tick only when the caller gave an onPress (the tick is the outcome of a command); onLongPress ticks at the long press. This is a refinement of 'inside onPress'.
StaticPress or GivingPress is latched at mount from scaleTo === 1 (same R4 rule as Appear), so a scaleTo change never remounts the content.
Segmented: segments use the button rung. The already-selected segment gets haptic none. Scroll mode uses hapticOn release (my call; the plan only said to set it in Segmented).
usePressLift defaults to the row rung (0.985), not CARD_PRESS_SCALE (0.986, pinned by task-card-face.test); that constant moves when TaskCard adopts the hook.
Appear: the entrance object is latched at mount along with the element type, so a re-render can neither rebuild the entering prop nor swap the element.
afterLoading arrivals are capped at 6 rows; the rest of a long first page are baselined as seen. The initial view-key assignment does not baseline an afterLoading first list.

1.5.summary: The precondition fails, so I made the change: the owner's HONOR is 361 dp at font scale 1.15, not 1.3. TaskCard no longer reads the window width. It stacks its head and foot only when useLayoutClass().stacked is true (window under 340 dp, or text scale 1.3 and up). Before, it stacked under 380 dp, so the phone never drew the designed layout. ApplicationFace used to stack only on scale (it never read the width, so the HONOR already drew its baseline offer row, as new_mp_sve.png shows). It now uses the same hook, so it also stacks under 340 dp. What the owner sees on the phone: the foot is one row, with the person and the places side by side instead of on two rows (about 34 dp shorter per card, by my arithmetic); on his own tasks the note and the 0/1 count share a row (about 15 dp). A task with an amount and a short title (about 20 characters or fewer) gets the price beside the title (8 to 17 dp shorter). Not changed: titles over 42 characters, 'Tražim ponude' and 'Cena nije navedena' still stack the head under CardHead's own rule. The 62-character sample card in w5_zadaci.png therefore keeps its stacked head; only its foot rule changes, and that foot has only the count. The 190-210 dp target is NOT reached by this flip. Pin card (DiscoveryPeek builds its own face) is untouched. 320 dp and text scale 1.3 still stack completely. The accessibility sentences, command names and hints are identical in every layout.
1.5.tests: EVIDENCE ARITHMETIC (w5_zadaci.png, 1264x2728 px, HONOR 2026-10-02 00:29). (1) px per dp: the Zadaci list pads cards 20 dp (DiscoveryPresentation list uses sys.space.lg) and the card's left edge is at x=70 px, so 70/20=3.5 px per dp. The Mapa pill is minHeight 48 and measures 168 px, so 168/48=3.5. That is 560 dpi, matching the R16-R19 receipts. Window = 1264/3.5 = 361.1 dp. (2) Font scale: the capital P of the 16 sp fact 'Petrovaradin' (Inter Medium, cap height 1490/2048=0.7275 em; read from the bundled TTF) measures 47 px, with 48 for the digit 0 and 47 for the A of 'Automobil'. Predicted cap height is 16x3.5x0.7275 = 40.7 px at 1.0, 46.9 px at 1.15, 53.0 px at 1.3. 47 px therefore means 1.15, and 1.3 is excluded by 6 px. The 20 sp title P/N measure 56 px against 50.9 at 1.0 and 58.5 at linear 1.15, i.e. about 1.10, which fits Android's non-linear scaling of large sizes at 1.15. (3) Independent witnesses: ApplicationFace stacks its offer only at scale 1.3 or more, and new_mp_sve.png shows 'Tvoja ponuda' beside the amount. Repo receipts say 'existing font scale 1.15 unchanged' on 2026-09-22 and in R16 to R19 on 2026-09-25. Result: layoutClassFor(361.14, 1.15) = compact, not stacked, so the flip is warranted. (4) Calibration of the amount estimate: '2.000 RSD' measures 106.3 dp of ink on the phone, and the Inter-metrics estimate at linear 1.15 is 120.9 dp, so the estimate is about 14 percent wide, on the safe side. COMMANDS AND RESULTS. Before the change the new test failed 17 of 77 (the flip cases, the amount-keeps-width cases at 340 and 361, the stack-at-320 and 339.9 application cases, the source guard, and one tolerance error of mine that I fixed). After the change: npx jest task-card-layout-class task-card-face application-face task-card-urgency gave 4 suites, 158 of 158 pass. npx jest task-card-layout-class task-card-face application-face one-token-source gave 4 suites, 233 of 233 pass. 24 related suites that render these cards (marketplace, own-tasks, own-applications, discovery map/route/spatial, peek-overflow, list-rows-memoized, press-reduced-motion, agreement-collection, text-scale, one-token-source and others) passed 24 of 26 in one run. The two that failed were 5 s timeouts under load: marketplace-presentation passed alone (21 of 21) and state-view passed alone (19 of 19). discovery-presentation timed out at 5 s on 9 tests under load and passed 159 of 159 with --testTimeout=90000. npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json found 2 errors, both in src/ui/system/__tests__/fact-art.test.tsx (another author's in-progress item 1.3 file), and none in my files. AMOUNT-FIT TEST (new file; real Inter advance widths read from assets/fonts/inter, digits at the widest digit, size = sp x scale, with 20 dp list padding, 1 dp border and 20 dp body padding). The widest amount CardHead puts beside a title is '888.888 RSD' at 20 sp bold. At 340, 361, 390 and 411 dp and scale 1, 1.15 and 1.29 it is always narrower than the row. Title column beside it, in dp, at scale 1 / 1.15 / 1.29: 340 dp gives 113 / 93 / 74; 361 dp gives 134 / 114 / 95; 390 dp gives 163 / 143 / 124; 411 dp gives 184 / 164 / 145. The test asserts a floor of 80 dp up to scale 1.15 (minimum 92.8). My offer row ('999.999 RSD' at 17 sp, plus 12 dp gap, plus the 24 dp art slot, 8 dp gap and the word 'ponuda') needs 215 / 241 dp against 266 to 337 dp of room at scale 1 / 1.15. The test also renders the real cards at each compact window and asserts the amount keeps flexShrink 0, has no maxWidth and no numberOfLines.

1.3.summary: Not seen on the phone: the icons were rendered only in desktop headless Chrome, and the dizajn-tabla board has not been opened in a build. What the owner will see once a build exists: icons at 24 px and below (79 of the 139 call sites, e.g. card rows at 16 and 20) become flat marks. A mark is one green plus white, with no ground shadow, edge or shine, strokes of 2.4 units or more, and no tone lighter than 3:1 on white. Sizes 25 and above (Profil rows 26, Home 32, tab bar 30, StateView 56) keep the sticker; the cut is chosen by size, so no call site was edited. Colour is one tone rule: every kind is the UI green (sys.color.art.brand, which is sys.color.green); the bell, the star and the new alert default to orange; `muted` still works and means the quiet grey. The old per-kind orange list and the lighter emerald #079C77 are gone, and the sticker is single-tone too. Calendar, tasks and remote no longer carry a tick; only check, agreements and shield do. 'offers' is now a price tag (no longer a chat bubble). New kinds: alert (triangle), publish (sheet with a plus badge) and send (paper plane). The calendar mark is a body, header band, two rings and two lines. The users mark is two people side by side, both in full tone. FACT_MEANING gives one phrase per kind. ICON_SYSTEM.md documents the three registers, both cuts, the tone rule and each drawing in words and coordinates. The board shows the ladder 16/20/24/32/48/64 for all 30 kinds, then 'Pre (levo) i posle (desno)' (sticker beside mark at 16/20/24), then the four tones. B22 cost: the mark uses 72 SVG shapes across the 30 kinds against 203 for the sticker, at most four per icon and always fewer than its sticker.

decisions: Cut threshold: 24 and below is the mark, 25 and above is the sticker, so Profil rows (26) keep the sticker, as ICO-02 says; the item text said 28 and above. Stated in the doc.

`size` stays a plain number: call sites pass 14, 18, 22, 26, 28, 30, 36, 40, 56 and 72 as well as the ladder, and typing it to FactSize would have forced edits in about 57 files. FACT_SIZES and FactSize are exported for new code.
Default tone by kind: bell, star and alert are accent (orange), everything else brand. Otherwise a rating star would turn green at every call site.

Accent in the mark cut uses the tone's edge (#C86821, 3.85:1) because its front (#FA8229) is 2.5:1 and fails the 3:1 floor. Rating stars and bells at 24 px and below are therefore a darker burnt orange than before.
`muted` is an alias of tone 'quiet' and wins over `tone`.

The sticker is single-tone as well: the second-hue details (orange calendar header, tasks badge, clock arc) are gone. This follows the owner default for this wave. The old two-tone is not restorable without redrawing.
Calendar and tasks stickers lost the checkbox and badge; the tasks badge now belongs to publish. The remote screen shows a person (a video call) instead of a tick.
'alert' defaults to accent: the plan calls it warning/needs-you, and an error picture passes tone danger or muted.
Rounded polygons are drawn with their own round-join stroke (offers, alert, send, star) instead of arc paths; the bounding-box test counts the stroke, so the painted extent is checked.
Round caps on white cut-throughs would show as nubs on a grey well, so the support bands and toolbox seam use butt caps (a `knock` helper) and the map creases are filled slits.
Drawings are built once per kind, tone and cut and shared (a small Map), to cut JS work in long lists.
The board's 'Pre' column draws cut='art' at 16/20/24. That is the old sticker's construction, not byte-identical: tones and ticks have already changed.

FactArt.tsx still spells about 20 neutral hexes (paper greys, ink) in the sticker; only the tone hexes moved to sys.color.art. The mark cut spells only the tone face and white. FactArt was not added to the colour-scope guard, because that test file is not mine.
notVerified: Nothing was seen on a phone. The marks were rasterized only in desktop headless Chrome at 3x from the real drawing code. I looked at the ladder, the 128 px geometry, 6x crops of the tricky kinds, and a grey well. PNGs are in the scratchpad: fa/small.png, fa/mark128b.png, fa/art128.png, fa/ladder.png, fa/crop.png, fa/crop2.png. Android react-native-svg anti-aliasing of 1.2 px strokes may differ.
Whether each kind is nameable without its word at 16 px at arm's length on the HONOR, and the 1.3 text-scale check, are phone checks. The gap of 3 units between details was judged by eye, not tested.
The B22 benefit (fewer SVG nodes per card) is counted, not measured on a device.
dizajn-tabla.tsx was only type-checked and covered by a source-text guard; it was never rendered. Wrapped rows at 320 dp are untested.
The full --findRelatedTests set (about 123 suites) was not completed; only the 27 named suites plus the two system suites ran.

Not wired, because those files are not mine: StateView still draws 'info' for errors and offline (alert is available); inboxEventArt; the Home publish door; the 'Termin nije potvrđen' status; the tab bar's inactive state; Glyph and StatusMark; call-site sizes 14/18/22/26/28/30/36 to the ladder.
risks: 79 call sites change look at once from sticker to flat mark, and the 54 sticker sites change tone, so this is an owner-visible redesign on every list screen. The owner A/B of single-tone against the old 2026-09-22 two-tone is only possible on the board.
Tests in other items that assert FactArt internals would break. The 27 suites run here pass, but concurrent edits to task-card-face, application-face and TaskCard by other items were not isolated.
Accent mark faces (bell, star, alert at 24 px and below) are darker than the brand orange, which may read brownish next to the vivid orange sticker at 25 px and above.
The tab bar still draws the 30 px sticker in quiet grey (#8F8F8F/#525252), so the 'dirty grey tab' complaint stays open until its item lands.
The 24 to 25 px boundary shows a visible style jump (flat to sticker), by design. A 24 px icon next to a 26 px one on the same screen would look inconsistent until call-site sizes are normalised.
The call-site scan (139 sites, 57 files, 18 `muted` sites) was regex-based and may miss unusual JSX forms.

reviews.summary:
I found no regression and no blocker. Wave 1 (items 1.2 to 1.5) is mergeable after a few small guard-quality and documentation fixes; the one with real consequence is the first below.

**What I ran** (all read-only on the checkout; mutations only on a scratch copy):
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: exit 0, no errors. The 1.4 author's two type errors in `fact-art.test.tsx` are gone.
- Primary suites (`src/ui/system/__tests__`, `src/ui/__tests__`, `task-card-layout-class`, `task-card-face`, `application-face`): 31 suites, 652 tests, all pass.
- Every suite found by `--findRelatedTests` for Press, Appear, Segmented, usePressLift, FactArt, ProductSheet, TaskCard, ApplicationFace and `dizajn-tabla`: 125 further suites, 2684 tests, all pass. This includes the heavy discovery suites, with a 120 s timeout and no load failures.
- Six more suites that depend only on tokens, textScale or motion (build-identity, entry-intro-hook, password-recovery-surface, system-reduced-motion-hook, map-appearance, map-style): 63 tests, all pass.
- Total 162 suites, no failures. I did not re-run the roughly 11 remaining suites that only import `tokens.ts` through another module.

**Do the guards fail when violated?** I ran 11 rounds, about 35 deliberate mutations, on a scratch copy; the checkout's git status was unchanged. Almost all mutations turned the right suite red:
- PRESS_DELAY set to 0, default `hapticOn` flipped to `in`, and the Press mount-latch removed.
- Tick without `onPress`, tick after `onPress`, long-press tick removed, and reduced motion ignored in `usePressLift` (give and settle).
- Appear: latch removed, `afterLoading` allowed at any time, and the six-row cap on arrivals removed.
- FactArt: mark cut limit moved to 28, a tick added to the calendar, a second emerald as brand, a fifth shape in the pin, a thin clock stroke, a duplicate meaning phrase, the accent mark drawn in the light orange, and the alert default tone dropped.
- Tokens: quiet tone too light, `sheetSpring` damping 20, press-ladder row rung 0.99.
- Layout class: narrow width 380, unrounded 1.2999 scale, and `useLayoutClass` ignoring the font scale.
- TaskCard always stacked or stacked only on `large`, and `ApplicationFace` losing the forced layout.
- A new file spelling `scaleTo={0.9}`, `Dimensions.get` or `duration: 200`.

What survived is in the findings: stale ratchet entries, a stagger cap with no test, a ternary `scaleTo` literal, an aliased `useWindowDimensions` import, and a constant not named `*PRESS_SCALE`. One more survivor (`Number.isFinite` in `layoutClassFor`) is an equivalent mutant: a NaN width does not stack either way.

**Other checks:**
- **File scope.** The union of modified and untracked wave-1 files matches the four authors' lists. During my review the B22 agent committed its own work (221e882e: package.json with `patch-package`, patches, workflow, scope.cjs, the B22 docs). That commit contains no wave-1 file, and the tree now holds exactly the 21 wave-1 files. No D12 file is dirty, and no new dependency comes from wave 1.
- **Entry and mascot files.** The checkout has no change to any entry, mascot or Home illustration file. Press tick timing (EntryWelcome buttons) and FactArt hue (Home rows at size 32) change indirectly, so the phone check should look at them.
- **Line endings.** The index is LF everywhere. In the working copy `FactArt.tsx`, `fact-art.test.tsx` and `textScale.ts` are LF while the rest of the repo's working files are CRLF. That is harmless with `autocrlf=true` (git only warns). `git diff --check` is clean, with no trailing whitespace and no BOM.
- **FactArt call sites** (138 JSX sites): all kinds used exist. The cut is picked by size, so no call site needed an edit, and the dynamic-size sites (Avatar 20/24/32, ContextPhotos, ProductDetails, DiscoverySearchPanel) land sensibly. Sizes 25 to 28 keep the sticker; the plan text said 28 and above, and the author stated this deviation.
- **Press literals.** Every `Press` call with a literal `scaleTo` is covered by an allow-list entry, except the ternary in PickerTile (see below).

**Not proven (stated, not inferred):** nothing in wave 1 has native or phone evidence. The 361 dp at font scale 1.15 precondition of item 1.5 rests on screenshot arithmetic, because plan item 1.1 (`wm size` and `font_scale`) was not run. It is safe either way: at 1.3 or more `useLayoutClass` returns `large` and the card stacks as before. The 340 to 379 dp compact window is newly exposed and is only arithmetic-tested, not rendered natively.

findings.issue: The two ratchets are billed as 'can only shrink' and 'lower or delete the entry in the same change', but the guards are ceilings (`found > allowed`, `readers ⊆ list`), not equalities. Items 1.4 and 1.5 of this same wave removed the work the entries were for, and the entries are now stale. `TaskCard.tsx` no longer reads the window width, yet it is still listed (line 337). `Segmented.tsx` no longer spells a press-scale literal, yet it still has `{ scale: 1 }` (line 414). Confirmed with a script: width readers actual 18 vs listed 19, and motion entry `Segmented: allowed 1, found 0`. Re-adding `scaleTo={0.98}` to Segmented leaves `one-token-source` green; only an unrelated press-reduced-motion test catches it. The counts in the comments and docs are also wrong: '19' should be 18, and '31 files' is actually 30 entries and 29 real ones.
findings.fix: Remove `'src/ui/v2/TaskCard.tsx'` from `WINDOW_WIDTH_READERS` and `'src/ui/system/Segmented.tsx'` from `MOTION_LITERALS_ALLOWED`. Make both guards exact: assert `[...WINDOW_WIDTH_READERS].filter(p => !readers.includes(p))` is `[]`, and for every listed file and family assert `found[family] === allowed[family]`, with a message 'lower this entry'. That makes shrinking mandatory. Correct the counts in the comments at lines 315 and 388 and in DESIGN_SKILLS.md lines 156 and 159.

findings.issue: Three blind spots, found by script and by mutation. (a) `src/ui/system/PickerTile.tsx:42` has `scaleTo={list ? 0.99 : 0.97}`: two press-scale literals that the regex (bare `scaleTo={0.9x}` only) cannot see and that no allow-list entry covers. This contradicts 'every Press call with a literal scaleTo is listed'. (b) An aliased import, `import { useWindowDimensions as useWin } ...; const dims = useWin(); dims.width`, passes the width guard (mutation A3: the width test stayed green). (c) A press-scale constant not named `*PRESS_SCALE` (e.g. `GIVE = 0.96`) is not detected.
findings.fix: Widen the scale pattern to something like `/\bscaleTo=\{[^}]*?\b0?\.\d+/g` and add `'src/ui/system/PickerTile.tsx': { scale: 2 }` to the allow-list. Make the width guard also flag `useWindowDimensions\s+as\b` and any `.width` read on an aliased binding, or forbid the identifier outside textScale.ts and the list. State the remaining limits in the test comment, as the author already did for the text-width test.

findings.issue: The stagger cap `Math.min(index, ROWS_THAT_ARRIVE) * sys.motion.stagger` is not pinned by any test. Mutating it to `index` left all five suites green (round R3: appear.test passed). Rule R4 ('at most six rows') therefore holds only for the number of animated views, not for the delay. A 40-row first page would get an unbounded delay without any test failing.
findings.fix: Add a test that the row at index ROWS_THAT_ARRIVE + 4 gets the same `entering` delay as the row at index ROWS_THAT_ARRIVE (read it from the mocked FadeInDown chain, or export the `arrival(index)` helper and assert on it).

findings.issue: The section 'Pre (levo) i posle (desno)' is described as 'left is how the card looked'. The left column is `cut="art"`, which is now the new single-tone sticker, not the old two-tone sticker with orange per kind and the lighter emerald. So the board cannot show the owner the before. UIUX_PLAN conflict 3 required the orange decision to be 'shown to the owner as an A/B first', and the author's reply says the old two-tone art is not restorable without redrawing. The A/B is therefore only possible from the old screenshots (base_home etc.) or from git.
findings.fix: Relabel the section to what it is ('Nalepnica (art) | Oznaka (mark)'), fix the comment, and state in ICON_SYSTEM.md that the true before is in the BEFORE screenshots and in git history. Tell the owner that the single-tone sticker was a decision made for him in this wave, with no A/B yet.

findings.issue: The header says 'every colour here comes from sys.color.art' and plan item 1.2 aimed at FactArt no longer owning hex values. Tone colours do now come from the tokens, but the art cut still has 21 distinct hand-written hex literals (about 33 uses): #163D2B, #D6DAD6, #CCD4CE, #C5CDC7, #7B887E, #35463D, #056B4D and others. The claim is false as written.
findings.fix: Reword the header and the doc to 'every tone', and list the neutral literals as a known remainder (a later pass can move them to tokens), or move them to named `sys.color` neutrals now.

findings.issue: The existing JSDoc ('A row arriving in a list', ending '`useAppear()` belongs to the list, not to the row') is now followed by the `ROWS_THAT_ARRIVE` constant instead of `useAppear`, so `useAppear` has no doc and the file header floats over the wrong declaration.
findings.fix: Move the header comment to a file-level comment above the imports or onto `useAppear`, and keep the `ROWS_THAT_ARRIVE` doc as its own block.

findings.line: art block (about line 130), and `sys.art` near the top
findings.issue: There are now two things called `art` in the token tree: the old `sys.art` (HomeIllustration drawing colours) and the new `sys.color.art` (fact-picture tones). `one-token-source.test.ts` has to iterate both (`colourLeaves(sys.color)` and `colourLeaves(sys.art)`). This is a trap for the next author.
findings.fix: Rename the new group (for example `sys.color.fact`) before later waves adopt it, or add a one-line note on both declarations. A rename costs only FactArt.tsx, one test and the docs today.

findings.issue: Documented deviations from the plan to carry as open items: `push` stays 280 instead of 240, `springSheet` is not deleted (DiscoveryMap still reads it), `pressDelay` lives in Press.tsx instead of `sys.motion`, and `SHEET_SPRING` is still an alias in ProductSheet. All are explained in the code and the author replies and are consistent, but nothing tracks them for the later waves.
findings.fix: Add them as explicit 'to do in wave N' lines in the wave-1 closure note or the control row, so a later item removes them (`springSheet` with DiscoveryMap, `push` with the transition item, `PRESS_DELAY` into `sys.motion`, the `SHEET_SPRING` alias with the sheets).

findings.issue: Inherited behaviour change that touches locked or sensitive surfaces. `EntryWelcome.tsx:111` (locked entry, `Press scaleTo={1} haptic='light'`) now ticks on release instead of on touch-down, and every card's `onPressIn` (the give) arrives 60 ms later. This is the intended wave-1 change and no locked file was edited, but 'preserve the entry timing' should be confirmed on the device rather than assumed. Home rows at size 32 also change hue (calendar and people from orange to green).
findings.fix: Add the entry buttons and the Home rows to the 'verifyOnPhone' list for wave 1 (tick on release, no dead feeling on a quick tap, Home hue). Keep the status SOURCE/CI until the HONOR evidence for the exact build exists (AGENTS 3.2.4).

reviews.lens: DOES IT ANSWER THE OWNER AND OBEY THE RULES (wave 1, items 1.2-1.5)
reviews.summary:
I read the plan and audits and the owner's complaints, and reviewed the git diff of src/ui plus the three docs and board, read-only. I re-ran `tsc --noEmit` (clean, no errors) and 7 core suites (429 tests green). The foundations (1.2), the Press/Appear rework (1.4) and the 361 dp / 1.15 evidence for 1.5 hold up. Two things need fixing before the first APK. (1) Item 1.5 opens the card head's price-beside-title layout to 340-379 dp phones without retuning its length gate (the 42/12-character rule was tuned for 380 dp and up). On a phone shaped like the owner's, some Moji zadaci cards get a narrower title column, a taller head, and mid-word breaks. The Zadaci list itself is not affected. (2) The dizajn-tabla 'Pre/posle' section is not a before/after, and the doc calls team defaults 'owner defaults'.

WHAT THE OWNER WILL SEE (none of it was seen on the phone).
- 1.2: nothing visible. Tokens, a layout-class hook, written colour and motion rules, ratchet tests, and a one-line alias in ProductSheet.
- 1.3: roughly 79 of 139 icon call sites (24 dp and below) become flat single-green marks. Calendar, tasks and remote lose their ticks. The orange and the lighter emerald disappear: Home rows, Profil rows and the tab bar keep the sticker but turn deep green. 'offers' becomes a price tag. Orange remains only for bell, star and alert.
  - I rendered old and new at 3.5x, which is the HONOR's 560 dpi. The marks are clean and legible at 16/20/24: no clipping, no hairlines, no ticks left. Silhouettes are distinct, though the map mark reads a little like an 'M' or 'III'.
- 1.4: no tick or shrink when a scroll starts on a card. The tick moves to the end of the tap, and the give starts 60 ms after the finger lands. Segmented ticks the moment a finger lands on a segment that would change. Settled list rows no longer carry a Reanimated view.
- 1.5: only TaskCard changed visibly. In the Zadaci list the foot becomes one row (person left, 0/2 right), about 34 dp shorter per card. That list passes `compact`, which still forces its head to stack, so the 190-210 dp target is not reached, and the author says so. On Moji zadaci the head can now put the price beside the title. ApplicationFace already drew the baseline layout on the HONOR, so it changes only under 340 dp.

PHONE-SCALE ARITHMETIC. It is sound: 1264 px / 3.5 = 361.1 dp, and 47 px cap height at 16 sp points to text scale 1.15, not 1.3. The layout class is therefore 'compact', and the owner's phone really was on the stacked side before. It still rests on a screenshot, not on `adb shell settings get system font_scale` (item 1.1 was not in this batch).

NO ENTRY, MASCOT OR HOME-SIGNATURE REGRESSION. No entry file is touched, HomeLaunchArt is untouched, and the Home 'Čeka te' rows keep their orange attention dot. No dependency or server change in wave 1.

findings.issue: The stacking rule was tuned for 380 dp and up: stack only if title.length > 42 or amount.length > 12. Item 1.5 now applies it unchanged to 340-379 dp phones. I simulated it with the repo's real Inter Bold advance widths at 361.14 dp, effective scale 1.10 (the repo test's own method). The title column beside the amount is about 150 dp for '5.500 RSD', 135 dp for '12.000 RSD' and 121 dp for '120.000 RSD'. In that simulation, 'Prevoz nameštaja do Petrovaradina' (33 chars) takes 4 lines and 'Petrovaradina' breaks mid-word, versus 2 lines stacked. 'Čišćenje stana posle renoviranja' with '120.000 RSD' takes 5 lines and breaks 'renoviranja', versus 2 stacked. With the same title lengths, the side-by-side head is taller than the stacked one in 1 of 10 cases at '5.500 RSD', 4 of 10 at '12.000 RSD' and 6 of 10 at '120.000 RSD'. The new test only asserts a column of at least 80 dp (about six letters), so it passes for these. The repo's R16 report says price-beside-title applies 'when space permits', and its own review calls 361 dp / 1.15 a compressed phone. Zadaci is not affected, because DiscoveryPresentation passes `compact` and `large || compact` still stacks its head. Moji zadaci own-task cards are (MarketplacePresentation does not pass `compact`). The claimed '8 to 17 dp shorter' only holds for titles of about 20 characters or fewer with a small amount.
findings.fix: Make the beside-gate depend on the room, not on a fixed length. Either have useLayoutClass expose a 'roomy' flag (width >= 380 dp and scale < 1.3) that keeps the 42/12 rule, with a stricter rule for compact-but-not-roomy (for example title.length <= 24 and amount.length <= 10, and no word over about 9 letters). Or measure with onTextLayout and fall back to stacked. Add a test that wraps realistic Serbian titles ('Petrovaradina', 'renoviranja', 'Električar za zamenu osigurača') with the Inter metrics already in task-card-layout-class.test.tsx and asserts that no word breaks and that beside is never taller than stacked.

findings.issue: The 'Pre (levo) i posle (desno)' section, captioned in code as 'left is how the card looked', draws the left side with `cut="art"` in the NEW tones. That is the new single-green sticker with no orange, no emerald and no ticks, not the old look. The old two-tone, which the owner approved on 2026-09-22, can no longer be shown anywhere. The plan's needsOwner item 1 calls for an A/B on this board before the colour reversal, and the four-tone strip only shows the new tones. DESIGN_SKILLS.md then says 'Two owner defaults were decided for this wave'. These are team defaults from the plan's needsOwner list, not owner decisions; he has not seen them. AGENTS 1.1 says never turn a proposal into approval, and 3.2.4 says evidence must be honest.
findings.fix: Keep the legacy two-tone for the board only: a board-local legacy drawing or static captured images of the old stickers, so left really is the old card. Otherwise rename the section ('sticker u novim tonovima / flat mark') and drop 'before'. Reword the doc to 'team defaults awaiting the owner's A/B on the phone'.

findings.issue: tokens.ts and DESIGN_SKILLS.md define green as 'a fact that IS confirmed, never a thing that is not true yet' and muted as 'a term that is not set'. The calendar fact is always drawn green. A flexible or absent schedule (item.schedule null, vremeTekst fallback) therefore still wears the green of a confirmed fact. Only the tick was removed.
findings.fix: Pass tone="quiet" (or muted) to the calendar FactArt when the term is flexible or unset, in TaskCard and the other calendar rows. Or soften the table so it does not promise this.

findings.issue: The small mark cut draws the accent with sys.color.art.accent.edge (#C86821, burnt orange). The sticker and the rest of the app use #FA8229. The same bell or star is therefore a different orange at 24 dp and at 26 dp, and the app now has two oranges. On the 3.5x render the mark reads brown. Rating stars at 14 px and bells turn visibly darker than before.
findings.fix: Pick one accent for both cuts. Either a single orange that passes 3:1, used by mark and sticker, or keep #FA8229 for the sticker and the board but draw the mark accent with a hex that reads orange rather than brown. Show it on the A/B card.

findings.issue: The comments in tokens.ts and DESIGN_SKILLS.md say 'a picture never owns a hex of its own'. FactArt.tsx still has 21 hand-written hex literals (greys such as #C5CDC7, #CCD4CE and #7B887E, ink #35463D, shadow #163D2B). #056B4D is a hair off sys.color.green (#076E4E), which tokens.ts itself says must use the token (CIEDE2000 <= 2.5).
findings.fix: Replace #056B4D with a token (art.brand.edge, or green at opacity). Move the neutral sticker greys and ink into one `sys.color.art.neutral` set, or reword both comments to say only the four tones are derived.

findings.line: header comment lines 16-18 (the premise); mark cut decision
findings.issue: The premise for the flat mark is stated in dp as pixels: 'the sticker detail is 0.5 to 1 px of noise at the 16 and 20 px the cards use'. The HONOR is 560 dpi, so a 16 dp icon is 56 device px and the sticker's edge (1.5 units) is about 2.6 px. In my 3.5x render the old 16, 20 and 24 stickers are clearly legible, not a smudge. The flat marks are cleaner, but the decision to drop 79 sites to flat marks is evidenced only by 1x desktop Chrome. It also reverses the sticker look the owner approved, and the cut changes abruptly at 24 vs 25 dp (24 dp rows next to 26-30 dp Profil, Home and tab-bar stickers).
findings.fix: State the premise in device pixels and say it is unverified on the HONOR. Put 16/20/24 at 560 dpi on the board in the first APK and let the owner choose. Consider a physical-pixel threshold only if the A/B favours the sticker.

findings.issue: The ratchets are not tight, although the doc says they can only shrink. TaskCard.tsx is still on WINDOW_WIDTH_READERS ('380') but item 1.5 removed its useWindowDimensions, so it can read the width again unnoticed. Segmented.tsx is allowed scale:1 but now has none (it uses sys.motion.scale.button). The comments say 31 files and the list has 30 entries. The 1.5 and 1.4 authors could not edit this file, so nobody lowered them.
findings.fix: Delete both stale entries. Add a check that a listed file still offends (found >= 1, and found == allowed for each family), so the list must shrink with the code. Correct the counts in the doc and comment.

findings.issue: In a non-scrolling Segmented the tick fires on touch-down (hapticOn 'in'), but the change is committed in onPress at release. A finger that lands on a segment and turns into a vertical page scroll still ticks and changes nothing. That is the same false tick rule R5 and item 1.4 set out to remove ('a tick belongs to a toggle or a confirmed result').
findings.fix: Default Segmented to hapticOn 'release' as well. Keep 'in' only where the control sits in a header that cannot scroll.

findings.issue: PRESS_DELAY (60 ms) applies to every Press that does not tick on touch-down, including primary buttons and sheet commands that sit nowhere near a scroll. A deliberate tap now begins to give 60 ms after landing, which can read as a slightly slower response. For a tap shorter than 60 ms, the give appears only after the finger lifts. A caller's `onPressIn`, including the card give(), also arrives 60 ms later. It is a hard-coded number, while rule R2 says every motion value is a token.
findings.fix: Apply the delay only to surfaces in a scrollable (cards and rows, for example scaleTo > 0.97 or an opt-in prop) and keep buttons at 0. Move PRESS_DELAY to sys.motion.pressDelay (the file Press.tsx comment already names as the next step).

findings.issue: Item 1.1 (read-only BEFORE probes: wm size/density, real font_scale, gfxinfo, 60 fps recordings) was not delivered, but the changes it was meant to baseline (press feel, haptics, card height) are. The 1.5 precondition rests on screenshot arithmetic. It is good arithmetic but indirect, and there is no BEFORE for jank or haptic counts.
findings.fix: Before the first APK, run the read-only probes in an owner-granted window. Record `settings get system font_scale` and `wm size/density`, plus the gfxinfo and 20-flick counts, so the AFTER on the HONOR has something to compare against.
